title: Lull-to-Lockstep Deploy Compact and Signal Epilogue - 2026-06
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact operational play and post-deploy epilogue for transitioning a traffic lane from a low-activity lull into a lockstep increase (staggered ramp to full rollout). It pairs a tight preflight checklist with a 48h watchlist and a lightweight communications template for customer-impact-sensitive features. Use this for small-to-medium feature rollouts where we need tight telemetry tuning and quick rollback options.

Context / When to use:
- Target audience: release engineers, on-call SREs, product owners during rollout hours.
- Ideal for feature gates that touch routing or model-selection logic (model routing, tiered-fallbacks, new quantization profiles).
- Not intended for massive infra-wide migrations or hardware swaps. For those use the full conductor runbook.

High-level plan (lockstep stages):
1) Hold window (T-72 to T-24): smoke tests, dependency freeze, comms ready.
2) Mini-canary (T0): 0.5% traffic to canary for 30m, validate functional and latency KPIs.
3) Staged ramp (T+30m to T+4h): stepwise increases 0.5%->5%->20%->50% with 30–60m observation at each step.
4) Lockstep align (T+4h to T+24h): if all checks good, expand to 100% in coordinated 2h window; otherwise pause and triage.
5) Epilogue (48h post-lockstep): final regression checks, ticket updates, and a short retro.

Compact preflight checklist (must be green before T0):
- Code/Config
  - Feature flag gated and tested in staging (flag name: feature.lockstep.<service>)
  - Backwards-compatible API contract verified (integration tests green)
  - Release artifact tag present and documented in PR body
- Infrastructure
  - Autoscaling thresholds and target utilization reviewed for new workload patterns
  - Canary instances provisioned in region(s) matching sampling population
  - Circuit-breaker thresholds and rate-limits reviewed with SRE (link in linked_artifacts)
- Observability
  - Dashboards: latency p50/p95, error rate, model quality regression metric, CPU/GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate pre-built and pinned
  - Traces: sampling enabled for canary requests (1:1k -> ramp if needed)
  - Alerting: elevated alert set for +200% error rate vs baseline OR +50ms p95 degradation for >10m
- Comms
  - Stakeholders notified in #deploys and primary on-call assigned
  - Customer impact template prefilled (see Communication Templates below)
- Rollback readiness
  - Clear rollback artifact (previous model tag / previous config commit) documented
  - Rollback owners assigned and briefed on steps (fast rollback, circuit backfill)

Mini-Canary Execution Notes (T0):
- Sample population: choose low-correlation segment (0.5% global, prefer region with representative traffic).
- Duration: minimum 30 minutes; extend if noisy signals present.
- Observations: manual confirmation on functional checks, and automated gating on metrics below.
- Gate metrics (automated):
  - ErrorRate_canary <= baseline*1.5 for 30m
  - Latency_p95_canary <= baseline_p95 + 50ms for 30m
  - ModelQuality_canary >= baseline - 1% (or feature-specific threshold)
  - GPU_utilization within provisioning buffer (no sustained >85%)
- Abort conditions: any gate fails or sustained noise in logs (exceptions spike >x10) -> immediate scale-down to 0% and start triage.

Staged Ramp Heuristics:
- Step sizes and dwell times are suggestions. Bias to smaller steps and longer observation for customer-facing features. Typical step pattern: 0.5% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100%.
- Before each step: confirm green on the immediate gate metrics and manual thumbs-up from on-call SRE for the next region/step.
- Use canary mirror traffic for extended load tests if available.

Rollback Decision Matrix (quick):
- Severity A (customer-visible outage or data corruption): immediate rollback to previous artifact + page on-call, pause releases in other regions.
- Severity B (significant latency regression >100ms p95 or sustained error rate increase >300%): step back to previous step for 30–60m, if no recovery rollback to previous artifact.
- Severity C (minor quality drift within tolerance or non-customer-facing logs): continue with caution, open an ops ticket and schedule a fix in next patch window.

48h Watchlist (real items we will monitor):
- Functional: 24h sample of user flows that previously had low coverage (quick smoke: onboarding, key API flows).
- Telemetry: token/time-based cost delta, KV cache hit rate, average batch sizes, tail latency (>99th percentile).
- Quality: small eval suite run every 6h vs predeploy baseline (automated job) and manual sample review by PM/ML lead inside 24h.
- Cost: GPU hours and egress delta compared to baseline week.
- Customer signals: support tickets tagged with feature name and Slack watches for escalation.

Communication Templates (short):
- #deploys initial post: "T0: initiating mini-canary for feature.lockstep.<service>. Sampling 0.5% region=us-west1. Owners: Marcus Li (release), Emily Chen (SRE). Watchlist: latency p95, error-rate. Linked artifacts: https://linear.app/RD-4821"
- Customer impact update (if needed): "We observed elevated error rates for X subset. Rolling back to previous config at +T0+56m. Customer-facing impact expected to be minimal; support team notified and investigating. Follow-up to come in ticket RD-4821."
- Post-epilogue summary (48h): "Rollout completed to 100% at T+6h. Key metrics: p95 latency +12ms, error-rate +0.3%. Post-deploy scoreboard and outstanding items: see below."

Run-of-day (operator timeline for first 8h):
- T-1h: final checks, brief handoff on Slack call, confirm alert thresholds
- T0: flip to 0.5% canary
- T+30m: confirm gates, ramp to 5%
- T+90m: confirm gates, ramp to 20%
- T+3h: confirm gates, ramp to 50%
- T+5h: decision checkpoint for 100% expansion or pause
- T+6–8h: expansion to 100% if green
- T+8–48h: passive watch with daily check-ins at +24h and +48h

Post-deploy Epilogue Checklist (to land the doc):
- Populate this doc with final metric snapshots
- Close or link Linear tickets created during rollout and tag with "deploy-epilogue"
- Short 15m retro with release owner, SRE, PM within 72h (capture: what surprised us, what to change in preflight)
- Update runbook (if a pattern repeated) and note parameter changes to gate thresholds

Open questions / Known risks:
- Sampling bias: are our sample regions representative for model routing changes? If not, add a regional preflight.
- Eviction/Cache warmup: new model variants may cold-start KV caches and increase latency for first users—recommend warmup traffic via synthetic requests during hold window.

Appendix: Quick links and snippets
- Rollback quick commands (ops):
  - rollback artifact: deployctl promote --to previous --service <svc> --region <r>
  - disable feature flag: ffctl set feature.lockstep.<svc> false --immediate
- Observability queries (examples):
  - p95 latency: sum(rate(request_duration_bucket[5m])) by (le) -> compute quantile
  - error-rate: sum(rate(request_errors_total[5m])) / sum(rate(requests_total[5m]))

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep comms crisp; reduce noise in #deploys by having a single signal owner post updates.
- For next iteration: automate the mini-canary gate evaluation (Slack bot thumbs-up) to save time on manual checks.

End of compact runbook. Fill in metric values post-rollout and tag action items before closing.
